description: Sabotages for win-etw-sys. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format and for why the results are read the way they are.
notCoveredHere: What only a trace session can show is not swept here: whether an event is enabled while a session listens, that the level and keyword filters hold, and that the descriptor and data reach the session as written are tests/session.rs, which are ignored without elevation (WE-D-3), so a sweep on a machine that cannot start a session would report a sabotage of those as surviving for a reason that is not a hole. They, and the activity ids an event is written with (WE-D-4), are sabotage-session.json, swept on a machine that can. A handle that is unregistered twice is not injected: the call would be made on a handle that is gone, and the sweep would be measuring a crash and not a test.

sabotages.name: WE-D-2: a GUID's second group is read back one bit off
sabotages.why: A GUID's value is one big-endian number, so each group is read from its own place; a shifted group reads back a value that is not the one given.

sabotages.name: WE-D-2: a terminated UTF-16 string has no terminator
sabotages.why: A decoder reads a UnicodeString to a zero unit, so a string without one runs on into the next field.

sabotages.name: WE-D-2: a terminated UTF-16 string is ended with one byte
sabotages.why: The terminator is a zero unit, two bytes; a one-byte terminator leaves the event's layout wrong for every field after it.

sabotages.name: WE-D-2: a terminated byte string has no terminator
sabotages.why: As for UTF-16: an AnsiString is read to a zero byte.

sabotages.name: WE-D-2: a boolean is true as zero
sabotages.why: A template's Boolean is four bytes, one for true and zero for false.

sabotages.name: WE-D-2: a block's size is cut to a ULONG and not refused
sabotages.why: A block longer than a descriptor's size can hold would be written as a short one; it is refused instead, and the call is not made.

sabotages.name: WE-D-2: a terminated string's blocks are written in reverse
sabotages.why: The blocks are concatenated in order, so a terminator before its string is a different event.

sabotages.name: WE-D-2: a registration is not unregistered when dropped
sabotages.why: A registration that is dropped must give its handle back, or a process that registers and drops runs out of its registrations; the limit test is the one that takes them all.

sabotages.name: WE-D-2: no fields are passed as a dangling pointer and not null
sabotages.why: The page allows UserData to be NULL when UserDataCount is zero, and the call refused an event with no fields that was given the pointer an empty vector holds.

sabotages.name: WE-D-2 control: a boolean is built by another spelling of the same conversion
sabotages.why: A control: the same value by another spelling, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.
